newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.S. grains council details Indonesia corn import.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grains council details Indonesia corn import.

text.p: The U.S. Feed Grains Council said on Wednesday Indonesia had imported nearly 665,000 tonnes of corn between January and September this year, mostly from the United States and Argentina.
An official from the council's Indonesian branch told Reuters imports in 1995 amounted to 1,087,813 tonnes.

Quoting figures culled from shipping and other sources by the council, the official said Indonesia had imported 308,223 tonnes from the United States between January and September 1996, compared with 797,300 tonnes for the whole of last year.
He said 290,500 tonnes were imported from Argentina in the same period compared with 163,500 tonnes in all of 1995. South Africa supplied 56,520 tonnes in the period against 69,000 tonnes in 1995.
There have been no imports from China this year, against 32,500 tonnes in 1995, the official said.
The official said that Indonesian imports during the U.S. 1995/96 fiscal year (Oct/Sept) totalled nearly 930,000 tonnes compared with 1,181,509 tonnes in 1994/95.
He said that among the main suppliers were the United States with 571,000 tonnes against 573,000; Argentina with 290,500 tonnes (160,000); South Africa 56,520 tonnes (253,000).
There were no corn imports from China in 1995/96 compared with 163,000 tonnes in the previous fiscal year.
The official said that soymeal imports between January and September this year totalled nearly 700,000 tonnes, with India accounting for 348,000 tonnes.
Among the other main exporters were Brazil with 218,500 tonnes; Argentina 75,000 tonnes and the United States 58,000 tonnes. He did not have comparative figures.
Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah had said Indonesia aimed to reduce its dependence on corn imports by planting the crop in an additional 500,000 hectares.
Corn was cultivated in 3.23 million hectares in 1995.
According to official data, local corn output rose by 19.7 percent to 8.2 million tonnes in 1995 over the previous year.
